newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 1997 growth forecast raised by Santander.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 1997 growth forecast raised by Santander.

text.p: Santander Investment on Tuesday raised its forecast for Mexican economic growth this year to 5.8 percent from 5.0 percent.

"Given expected higher public spending and a gradual recovery in real wages in the second half of the year, we expect the domestic sector to continue to grow at a solid pace in the coming months," economists Hector Chavez and Enrique Ramirez said in statement issued by the brokerage.
The upward revision was prompted by news on Monday that Mexico's gross domestic product grew 8.8 percent during the second quarter compared to the same quarter of last year.
That result was much stronger than expected, even though leading indicators, such as retail sales and second-quarter corporate results, had pointed to a robust commercial sector.
"Thus, an important share of the commerce sector's growth must be attributed to informal commerce," the report said.
